text:
alex: FYI: noticed a big uptick in preemptible evictions in us-west over the last 6h, ~28% eviction rate on p4d-preemptible nodes. Small-gen workloads saw 95p tail spikes and gateway retries.

maria: yikes. any cloud announced maintenance?

alex: nothing in maintenance logs. looks correlated with a short pricing spike — cloud-side spot reclaimers. evictions mostly for older-instance family.

jen: can we temporarily bias critical traffic away from preemptible? enterprise customers can't see retries.

paul: strong +1. suggest explicit routing policy: enterprise -> dedicated first, then region failover, then quantized model fallback. standard -> prefer preemptible but with quick fallback to dedicated. free -> cheapest preemptible-only.

sam: also want a soft policy for standard: preemptible-prefer but if estimated eviction_prob > 0.15 then spill to cheap dedicated. keep failover graceful.

alex: prototype routing rules I'm going to test:

```
# router pseudocode
if customer.tier == \"enterprise\":
  route_order = [dedicated-local, region-failover(dedicated), quantized-variant]
elif customer.tier == \"standard\":
  route_order = [preemptible-prefer, dedicated-burst, quantized-variant]
else:
  route_order = [preemptible-only, cheap-quantized]
# add eviction probability gating and egress/cost checks
```

maria: add a jittered spillover/backoff to avoid thundering herds when a whole pool is evaporating (randomized 20-80s).

jen: good call. when we cross-region fail, we must preserve model state. For chat sessions restrict context to <=1024 tokens for safe variant switch; otherwise we risk mismatched encodings.

paul: ops note: cross-region failover has egress and latency consequences. add a cost gate: only allow region-failover if projected egress cost per 100k reqs < X or if SLA tier is enterprise. I'll run numbers for 10k rps.

sam: infra-side: implement a 5m eviction-prob sampler that microbursts data into router decisions, and an instance draining hook that pushes KV-cache snapshots to vacuum-store for 30s before termination to speed resume on fallbacks.

alex: also add an oncall runbook step: when eviction rate > 20% in a region for > 15min, create incident with tag spot-churn and escalate to infra-oncall. include affected models and current router config.

oncall-bot: Incident created: CHURN-2026-042, assigned to infra-oncall. https://incidents.internal/CHURN-2026-042

jen: I'll mock a console toggle: \"allow-region-failover\" (off for standard by default, on for enterprise). tooltip shows estimated egress cost and latency impact.

paul: quick back-of-envelope for 10k rps: avg payload ~2KB -> ~20MB/s -> ~1.7TB/day -> inter-region egress costs ~ $1400-$1800/day depending on route. will refine with per-region rates.

maria: I'll build the model-compatibility matrix for fallback variants (quantized vs full, context limits, tokenizer compatibility). need to know which models can accept truncated contexts safely.

sam: also propose a router-level probabilistic spill: when eviction_prob is between 10%-20%, spill X% of new sessions to dedicated to keep steady-state cache warm. ramps reduce cold-start penalty.

alex: nice. checklist for next steps:
- implement eviction-prob sampler (sam)
- router: jittered spillover + probabilistic spill (sam)
- model compatibility matrix (maria)
- console toggle mock (jen)
- egress cost projection (paul)
- PRs + staging test with synthetic eviction generator (alex/jen)

jen: will run a staged rollout plan: staging test -> 1hr canary on 5% traffic -> 25% -> full. rollback if evictions > 10% or 95p latency exceeds baseline by 30%.

maria: for monitoring, add metric: fallback-rate-by-tier and egress-by-fallback to surface the cost impacts.

paul: I'll also add a budget guardrail in billing infra to alert when inter-region egress from failovers exceeds threshold.

alex: cool. i'll open the infra PRs and link them here. will also add runbook snippets for oncall.

sam: one more: for long-running sessions, prefer model-variant fallback over region fail for cost-sensitive customers; region fail reserved for enterprise or when local capacity totally unavailable.

jen: noted. I'll include that as a priority matrix in the UI help text.

alex: thanks team. testing tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
